segments: The sixth jubilee.
The Kings of the Persians.
[In the ... year] of Ochus the Persian,
and the eighth of Philip,
Alexander of Hellas {OCR?} was born,
and the name of his mother was Olympias.
After him, four years.
At this time the philosophers Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle were famous.
Now Plato died at the age of eighty-two years,
and Speusippus, his cousin, succeeded him in his place,
and not Aristotle.
For although he was his disciple,
yet he did not agree with his sect (doctrine),
especially opposing him greatly concerning the transmigration of souls from bodies to bodies.
At this time, Manasseh, the brother of Jaddus {OCR?} the high priest of the Jews, built a great temple on Mount Gerizim resembling the one in Jerusalem.
And Alexander, the son of King Philip, was taught by Aristotle {OCR?}.
For Socrates and Plato received wisdom {OCR?} from Pythagoras the Great.
And after Socrates died, then Plato became renowned.
And Theon of Alexandria counted thirty-three books that Plato composed,
among which are the book of Politicus,
and the book of Laws,
and the book of Phaedo,
and the book of Timaeus.
And through both father and mother, that Plato was of council (bouleutic) rank.
For his father was descended from Poseidon,
and his mother from Solon the lawgiver of the Athenians.
And others say that when Plato was a youth,
he was very skilled in poetry.
And when he went to Socrates,
and saw him despising that art,
he burned the books of poetry which he possessed,
and joined himself to Socrates,
and was his disciple for fifty {OCR?} years.
And from him he learned the Pythagorean wisdom {OCR?}. And when he died, he left several gardens, two slaves, one cup, a bowl,
and the earring which he used to wear in his ear in his childhood as a sign of his noble birth.
And the rest of his possessions he had spent on the betrothal of his brother's daughters,
and he had also distributed to his friends.
Now it was written upon his tomb:
"Here lies that divine man,
who surpassed all men in wisdom {OCR?}, modesty, and upright habits.
Therefore, whoever praises wisdom {OCR?},
to this [man...]"
